short: Conjugated dicarboxylate anodes for Li-ion batteries
title: Conjugated dicarboxylate anodes for Li-ion batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Safer and more sustainable low-voltage negative electrodes than lithiated graphite are needed. Weakly electron-withdrawing carboxylates as redox centres: losing carboxylate resonance (and core aromaticity) on 2Li/2e uptake should give low-potential redox.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/down_select), n4 (PRC/synthesis), n7 (PRC/forming), n8 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: Lithiated graphite LiC6 reacts strongly with electrolyte over 150-180 C (refs 14, 15)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Li uptake reduces both dicarboxylates, altering carboxylate and ring bonding in the discharged state. Li removal restores the pristine molecular structure: the redox is reversible for both salts

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Loss of carboxylate resonance (and, in terephthalate, of ring aromaticity) on reduction places Li uptake at low potential. Li uptake occurs on low-voltage plateaus: ~1.4 V for Li muconate and ~0.8 V for Li terephthalate.
states.detail: Absorbed: m0 (MEC/pathway), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value), n18 (PRP/value). Premises: Organic electrodes with quinone/phenoxide redox centres operate at higher potentials, suited to positives

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Capacity fades slowly on cycling to ~234 mA h/g after 50 cycles (terephthalate) and ~125 mA h/g after 80 cycles (muconate). Negatives based on 0.8 V Li terephthalate should give safer cells than graphite; 1.4 V Li muconate is safer than Li4Ti5O12
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (PRF/service_capability), n16 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Lithiated graphite LiC6 reacts strongly with electrolyte over 150-180 C (refs 14, 15); Li4Ti5O12, the usual safe alternative negative, works at 1.5 V with 150 mA h/g

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Conjugated Li dicarboxylates are reversible low-voltage organic anodes (0.8 V/~300 mA h/g; 1.4 V/~170 mA h/g) with much lower thermal reactivity than graphite
